metadata.description: Absolute hypsometric tint with an Igor hillshade over the GEM-15 terrain tiles built by the Mapterhorn pipeline. Cusco, Machu Picchu and the Salcantay massif, over 1 one-degree GEM-15 cell (wm73sm14), with 4,260 m of relief. Tiles exist from -73.125 to -70.3125 degrees east and -16.636 to -11.178 degrees north; elevation exists over the cell inside that. Zoom 13 is one level deeper than Mapterhorn publishes here today: its production aggregation holds nothing finer than 30 m GLO-30 over this cell. This is cloud forest, so part of what the extra detail shows is canopy rather than ground.
metadata.portolan:experiment: These tiles were built by running GEM-15 through the Mapterhorn terrain pipeline on an unmerged fork (cholmes/mapterhorn, branch gem-15-source, built at commit 86d8494), as a test for mapterhorn issue 368. They are not a Mapterhorn release and the Mapterhorn project has not endorsed them. The archive's own PMTiles metadata declares the pipeline's '© Mapterhorn' credit and nothing else, so this style sets the full attribution on the source, which MapLibre prefers over the archive's own metadata.
metadata.portolan:dtm-variant: This style draws the area's surface model (DSM), which includes canopy and buildings. The bare-earth model (DTM) for the same area is the sibling archive mapterhorn-gem15-cusco-dtm.pmtiles: same cells, same pipeline, same zoom range, pixel-aligned. Change the one url line under sources to render it instead, and change nothing else. No separate DTM style exists on purpose. The ramp, the hillshade, the tile size and the maxzoom are identical between the two bands, so a duplicate style would only be a second place to forget a ramp change. Expect the DTM to read at or a little below the DSM, by 5 m over the Barcelona Eixample and 0.5 m on bare rock at Montserrat, and expect no difference at all over filled voids such as the Sau reservoir, where both bands take the same Copernicus GLO-30 surface.
metadata.portolan:ramp: Stops in meters (EGM96): -430 #0f3d2e, -5 #1d5c42, 0 #5d7f93, 1 #2d6a3f, 100 #4e8c4a, 300 #7aa85a, 600 #a8c06a, 900 #cfcf7d, 1200 #e2cf8c, 1600 #d8b074, 2000 #c0905c, 2400 #a4744a, 2800 #8a5c3e, 3200 #745038, 3600 #6d5b50, 4200 #8a7d74, 4800 #a99d95, 5400 #c9c0ba, 6000 #e6e2df, 6800 #ffffff, 8849 #ffffff. This is the same absolute ramp as the gem-15 collection's hypsometric style and as this collection's thumbnail, so a colour means the same height across the whole catalog. The deliberate 0 m to 1 m step puts a hard edge between the water tone and the lowland greens.
metadata.portolan:caveats: Elevations are meters above the EGM96 geoid, not ellipsoidal heights and not EGM2008; apply a geoid correction before combining with other DEMs for altimetry. Surface model (DSM), not bare earth, so canopy and buildings shade as terrain. GEM-15's own voids, water plus a 9 m buffer among them, are filled from Copernicus GLO-30 before encoding, so an inland reservoir shades as a real water surface rather than as a 0 m pit; a filled pixel is GLO-30 at 30 m, not GEM-15 at 15 m. Terrarium has no nodata value, so everything outside the archive's own cells encodes as 0 m and renders as a flat plain at the water tone. The archive's PMTiles header declares the whole world as its bounds, which is a defect of the fork's bundle_area.py rather than a statement about coverage; a map opened away from the area below shows that flat plain instead of an empty map, so set the map's own maxBounds if that matters.

metadata.portolan:minimum-client: MapLibre GL JS 5.6.0 or newer, which is where the color-relief layer type was introduced. The hillshade-method property needs 5.5.0 or newer. The pmtiles:// URL needs the PMTiles protocol registered on the map, for example with maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new Protocol().tile).
